title: Dedicated Fleet Provisioning: intake triage bot, approval SLA negotiation, and capacity runway calculator
creator: Alyssa Chen
description: Build an end-to-end intake and approval flow for Dedicated capacity requests that reduces time-to-commit and improves allocation accuracy. This ticket covers three deliverables: (1) an intake triage bot that classifies requests into Standard / High-Throughput / Burst and suggests initial throughput and duration; (2) an approval negotiation UI that presents SLA options, auto-suggests fallback model variants and cost trade-offs for sales/onboarding reviewers; (3) a capacity runway calculator that simulates committed vs predicted usage over a 12-month horizon to flag potential overcommit or shortfalls. Goal is to reduce manual triage time by 60% and decrease onboarding errors that lead to on-call incidents.
acceptance_criteria: Intake triage bot correctly classifies 90% of historical requests in validation set
Approval UI surfaces at least three SLA packages with estimated monthly cost and latency percentile impact
Runway calculator produces a 12-month forecast and flags high-risk weeks with >20% chance of capacity shortfall
End-to-end flow has instrumentation: time-to-approval metric, number of manual edits to suggested throughput, and customer satisfaction score in first 30 days
success_metrics: Median time from request to signed commitment <= 5 business days
Reduction in manual throughput adjustments during onboarding >= 60%
Onboarding-related incidents attributed to provisioning < 1 per quarter
notes: We should avoid hard-coding model-level throughput recommendations; use a shim that maps workload patterns to recommended CU (capacity units) profiles.
Trade-off: conservative runway calc reduces risk but increases committed cost — allow configurable risk appetite per customer tier.

Prefer lightweight triage ML model (logistic reg / gradient boost) trained on request metadata and recent telemetry rather than full feature-parity with serving runtime models to keep inference cheap.
Constrain rollout to non-production customers initially, then expand via canary to customers with small reservations.
implementation_plan: Week 1-2: Data sprint — assemble historical intake forms, onboard usage telemetry, label dataset for triage categories
Week 3: Prototype triage model + simple API; build UI stub for intake form with suggested throughput
Week 4-5: Approval UI with comparison table for SLA/latency/cost and autosuggest fallback variants
Week 6: Capacity runway calculator service; integrate with forecasting baseline (moving-average + seasonality) and Monte Carlo risk sampling
Week 7: End-to-end integration testing, instrument metrics, and run internal canary
Week 8: External pilot with two customers, collect feedback, iterate
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Overly optimistic throughput recommendations that cause undersized fleets. Mitigation: default to conservative percentile (P90) and require manual confirmation for first two onboardings.
Risk: Approval UI complexity overwhelms sales. Mitigation: provide a compact default view and an expanded detail view for power users.
Risk: Forecast error during large seasonality events. Mitigation: allow manual override windows and label expected spikes during intake.
Risk: Security/data exposure in triage model. Mitigation: strip PII from intake payloads and run model in private tier with KMS-protected keys.
